overall: The AG found the committee's blanket withholding of 2009–2010 executive session minutes unjustified for several meetings, upheld it for ongoing grievance matters, and ordered a 30-day fresh review plus a public status announcement.

allegations.summary: Complainant (a newspaper) alleged the committee unlawfully kept FY2009 executive session minutes sealed, citing vague 'pending legal concerns', and asked that the purpose be deemed expired.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee has not provided us with any information justifying continued non-disclosure of the minutes from this executive session, therefore we find that the executive session purposes have expired.

allegations.summary: Whether continued withholding of the October 27, 2009 executive session minutes was justified, given the minutes show litigation, bargaining and grievance discussion.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee has not provided us with any information justifying continued non-disclosure of the minutes from this executive session, therefore we find that the executive session purposes have expired.

allegations.summary: Whether withholding the February 23, 2010 executive session minutes (grievance discussion) remained justified.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the executive session was appropriate under Purpose 3 as part of the collective bargaining process, and agree that this purpose has not yet expired because the grievance matter has not yet been resolved.

allegations.summary: Whether withholding the March 9 and March 23, 2010 executive session minutes was justified, given some grievance matters were resolved.
allegations.key_passage: It has, however, expired with regard to the matters that Attorney Cocuzzo stated have been resolved.

allegations.summary: Whether withholding the May 11, 2010 executive session minutes (grievance, litigation and bargaining matters) was justified.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee has not provided us with any information justifying continued non-disclosure of the minutes from this executive session, we find that the executive session purposes have expired.

allegations.summary: Whether withholding the June 8, 2010 executive session minutes (litigation, bargaining and personnel contracts) was justified.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee has not provided us with any information justifying continued non-disclosure of the minutes from this executive session, therefore we find that the executive session purpose has expired.

allegations.summary: Whether withholding the September 22, October 13, November 24 and December 8, 2009 minutes (a specific litigation matter) was justified.
allegations.key_passage: In light of that pending review, we decline to take a position on whether or not continued non-disclosure is warranted.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes before July 2010 did not state the purpose for entering executive session; the AG addressed whether that omission was unlawful.
allegations.key_passage: Prior to the date, the law required a public body to state the purpose for an executive session, though there was no clear requirement that the public body include that statement of purpose in its minutes.

remedy: Within 30 days, conduct a fresh review of all the unreleased executive session minutes listed in the letter to determine whether the executive session purpose justifying non-disclosure has expired.
After completing the review, make a public announcement at the next meeting regarding the status of each set of minutes, per G.L. c. 30A, § 22(g)(1).
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
